{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-sd-x","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"e1aa640826b9029c3e4f7565757abae6ddb3f05c6faa42f23c3f04715def8333","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-sd-class-std:lineage:73","source_registry_sha256":"a4e51960bfe4da242ea11046073ac8d3d0353ce120a5409a11c1f9ab4c4da57a","source_liveness_sha256":"1aea607665fc1312b9a6988c94545b32e414886d6d428b2b6d66e4261f9397f1"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing the road","heading":"C — Knowledge dossier: Sharing the road","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Knowledge dossier: Sharing the road

FACT_ID: sec17-F01 | anchor: A61
Share the roadway courteously and communicate location and intended movements to reduce crash risk. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F02 | anchor: A61
Be ready to yield to pedestrians even outside crosswalks, and yield at intersection crossings even when unmarked. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F03 | anchor: A61
Always yield to visually impaired people and stop completely for a crossing pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F04 | anchor: A61
Yield to pedestrians already in an intersection even when your light is green. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F05 | anchor: A61
A turn on red still requires readiness to yield to pedestrians. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F06 | anchor: A61
Near parked or stopped vehicles, slow and do not pass until sure no pedestrian is crossing ahead of them. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F07 | anchor: A61
Check for pedestrians before backing, particularly in parking areas with many people. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F08 | anchor: A61
In residential and playground areas, watch for children emerging between parked cars and be ready to stop, using a lower speed when appropriate. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F09 | anchor: A61
In school zones, obey the lower speed when warning lights flash or children are present, and stop or yield when crossing patrol signals it. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F10 | anchor: A61
A bicycle on the roadway is a vehicle whose rider shares motorists’ rights, privileges, responsibilities and road rules. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F11 | anchor: A61
Watch for cyclists because skill varies and an unpredictable rider may swerve, ignore controls or lack a night light. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F12 | anchor: A61
Yield to bicyclists in intersections and where a bike path or lane crosses a road. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F13 | anchor: A61
Do not stop, park or drive in a designated bike lane or path except for alley or driveway access, official duties, police direction or an emergency. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F14 | anchor: A61
Slow and give cyclists ample space, allowing a cyclist to clear the intersection before you turn. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F15 | anchor: A61
Avoid abrupt slowing or stopping in front of a bicycle because a motor vehicle’s stronger brakes can create a collision risk. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F16 | anchor: A61
Avoid sounding the horn close to a cyclist unless needed to avert a crash, because startling the rider may cause a swerve. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F17 | anchor: A61
Watch for cyclists entering the lane, especially children moving from a sidewalk into the road. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F18 | anchor: A61
Do not turn sharply across a cyclist’s path or force the cyclist off the road. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F19 | anchor: A61
Although cyclists must travel with traffic, look for riders anywhere on the roadway. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F20 | anchor: A61
Use extra care around cyclists on wet, sandy or gravel-covered roads because those surfaces affect bicycles more strongly. [A61]
Source: [A61 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec17-F21 | anchor: A62
Cyclists signal turns and stops by hand, but conditions may require both hands on the bars, so also watch head or shoulder looks for intent. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F22 | anchor: A62
Before opening a street-parked vehicle’s door, check beside and behind for bicycles. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F23 | anchor: A62
Check for bicycles before backing, particularly near schools and homes. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F24 | anchor: A62
For a same-direction bicycle pass at a posted limit of 35 miles per hour or less, allow at least 3 feet from the vehicle’s right side including projections to the bicycle’s left side. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F25 | anchor: A62
For that bicycle pass above a posted 35-mile-per-hour limit, allow a minimum of 6 feet. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F26 | anchor: A62
A safe bicycle overtake may partly cross the centerline or a same-direction lane line, and the required separation must last until safely past. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F27 | anchor: A62
The quoted Section 32-26-26.1 classifies a bicycle-passing violation as a Class 2 misdemeanor. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F28 | anchor: A62
A motorcycle has the same road rights and responsibilities as another driver and must receive a full lane width rather than a shared lane. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F29 | anchor: A62
Check mirrors and blind spots for hard-to-see motorcycles and scan front and sides before a left turn. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F30 | anchor: A62
Do not assume a flashing motorcycle signal means an imminent turn, because it may not cancel automatically; wait to confirm the rider’s action. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F31 | anchor: A62
Follow a motorcycle by at least 4 seconds and allow more time in wet conditions. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F32 | anchor: A62
Expect a motorcycle to change lane position for potholes, gravel, slippery patches, pavement seams, rail crossings or grooved pavement. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F33 | anchor: A62
Scooters and mopeds usually travel more slowly than motorcycles. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F34 | anchor: A62
The handbook reports more than 250,000 annual crashes between cars and commercial vehicles. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F35 | anchor: A62
Compared with cars, commercial vehicles generally maneuver less readily, have larger blind spots and need greater stopping, acceleration and turning room. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F36 | anchor: A62
The page’s loaded-truck example gives a stopping minimum of 290 feet at 55 miles per hour on a clear, dry road with good tires and adjusted brakes. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F37 | anchor: A62
The handbook says a bus may need at least 300 feet to stop. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec17-F38 | anchor: A62
No Zones include both places a car disappears from view and positions so close that a truck or bus cannot maneuver or stop safely. [A62]
Source: [A62 -> src:rdmv-sd-l:south-dakota-department-of-public-safety:handbook:pdf-0062]

Misconceptions: A bicycle is a roadway vehicle, a motorcycle needs the full lane, and large-vehicle mirrors do not eliminate No Zones. The text’s mention of a left turn on red does not establish permission for that turn.
Mnemonics: Use see, yield, space and communicate as an authored sharing-road cue.
Glossary: A No Zone is a large vehicle’s blind or unsafe close area; tail swing is rearward vehicle movement outward during a turn; a runaway ramp provides escape for vehicles unable to brake.
Dynamic facts: Road-user movements, bus departures and emergency scenes change continuously. Printed truck stopping and crash-count examples are not guarantees for every vehicle.
